newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end soft on Wall St, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end soft on Wall St, Brazil.

text.p: Ending a rollercoaster week, Chilean blue chips closed sharply lower for the second day in a row with the market pulled down by Wall Street's slide and renewed profit-taking in Brazil, said dealers.
But the turmoil should ease next week, allowing Chilean stocks to regain their footing ahead of company second-quarter results due at the end of the month, they said.
"The market should stabilize more next week, although investors will be taking positions as speculation about earnings grows," said one dealer.
The IPSA index closed down 1.13 percent at 129.98 points.
The general IGPA index shed 0.75 percent to 5,666.23 points.
Turnover shrank to 9.8 billion pesos from 11.3 billion pesos Thursday.
"The drop reflected the lack of real buyers. Foreign investors are still taking profits," said one dealer.
Top decliners included soft drinks bottler Andina dropped on concerns that any economic instability in Brazil could hit sales at its plant in Rio de Janeiro, said brokers.
Andina, Chile's largest Coca Cola distributor, dropped 2.51 percent to 1,560 pesos.
Among the losers, telecom Entel Chile SA were 1.86 percent lower at 3,165 pesos, and power utility Chilgener SA shed 1.75 percent to 168 pesos.
Gainers included pasta-maker Empresas Carozzi SA, up 1.09 percent at 465 pesos, and steel producer Cap SA , which rose 0.9 percent at 1,240 pesos.
